 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,

CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE E.S.INDIRESH  ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the Insurance Company assailing the judgment and award dated 19.07.2018, in MVC No.607/2015, on the file of learned II Additional NC: 2026:KHC-K:851 HC-KAR District and Sessions Judge, Bidar, sitting at Basavakalyan (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal'), awarding compensation to the claimants.

sentences.text: 2 2. For the sake of brevity, the parties in the appeal shall be referred to in terms of their status and ranking before the Tribunal.

3. It is the case of the claimants that, the wife of claimant No.1 - Surayya Begum was travelling in a Tempo-Trax bearing registration No.KA-35/7393 from Bidar to Pune along with other inmates and as to the negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle in question, the alleged accident occurred and as a result of the same, wife of claimant No.1 - Surayya Begum died.
Hence, the claimants have preferred MVC No.607/2015 seeking compensation.
4. On service of notice, the respondents have entered appearance and contested the matter on merits.
In order to prove their case, claimant No.1 examined NC: 2026:KHC-K:851 HC-KAR himself as PW.1 and produced 15 documents and the same were marked as Exs.P1 to P15.
The respondents have examined two witnesses as RW.1 and RW.2 and got marked seven documents and the same were marked as Exs.R1 to R7.

The Tribunal after considering material on record, by its judgment and award dated 19.07.2018, awarded compensation of Rs.9,66,000/- with interest at the rate of 9%
per annum and feeling agreed by the same, the Insurance Company has preferred this appeal.

5. Sri Sharanabasappa M. Patil, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant - Insurance Company argued that, the deceased was travelling in the private car, which covers the private package policy and as such, the owner of the vehicle in question has violated the terms and conditions of the policy by hiring the vehicle at the time of the accident.
Therefore, he sought for interference of this Court.
It is also argued by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant that,
award of interest at the rate of 9% per annum is on the higher side.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:851 HC-KAR 6.

Having taken note of the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant, it is not in dispute as to the death of the wife of claimant No.1 in the alleged accident occurred on 09.05.2015, in which the deceased was travelling as a gratuitous passenger in Tempo-Trax bearing registration No.KA-35/7393.

In that view of the matter, taking into consideration that the appellant - Insurance Company has contested the matter on merits before the Tribunal and also produced relevant documents, disputing the fact that the vehicle in question was taken on hire.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that, fastening liability on the Insurance Company to indemnify respondent No.1 is required to be interfered with in this appeal.

Following the declaration of law made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd., vs. Baljith Kaur and others reported in (2004) 2 SCC 1, wherein, it is held that the Insurance Company is to satisfy the claim of the claimants and thereafter to recover the same from the owner of the NC: 2026:KHC-K:851 HC-KAR vehicle, in which the deceased was travelling as gratuitous passenger.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., vs. Baljith Kaur and others reported in (2004) 2 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that view of the matter, I find force in the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant.
7. Taking into consideration the Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 9% per annum, which is on the higher side.

Therefore, the claimants are entitled for interest at the rate of 6% per annum,
which is prevailing instead of 9% per annum, as granted by the Tribunal on the compensation awarded.
